author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating to human — same workspace-architectural family as .2 (invite-uses atomicity), .3 (SpaceInvite manage_members), .4 (SpaceBan ban permission). All four propose new typed methods on ChatBackend; the right shape is to take them as a single architectural decision.

The proposed redeem_invite_code(&self, caller, code) method is most naturally MERGED with the redeem_space_invite proposal from .2 — both touch the invite redemption path. The unified signature suggested in .2 was:

  redeem_space_invite_by_code(caller, code, new_member: SpaceMember)
      -> Result<(account_id, space_id, uses, Space), BackendSetError>

That single typed method covers BOTH:
- (.10) global invite-code lookup (returns the account+space that owns the code, ignoring caller account_id)
- (.2) atomic uses-increment + member-add (single backend operation)

Recommendation: defer this bead. When the workspace decides on the .2/.3/.4 trait-shape family, .10 is folded into the same call and closed as a duplicate or co-fixed by the unified method.
